card.summary: 5 GB free for open-source projects: 'Users have a free 5 GB limit for open source projects and 20 Cachix Deploy agents.' Paid tiers start at 50 GiB.

free_tier.stated: 5 GB free for open-source projects: 'Users have a free 5 GB limit for open source projects and 20 Cachix Deploy agents.' Paid tiers start at 50 GiB.

egress.terms: Unlimited bandwidth even on the paid Starter tier ('Unlimited bandwidth', 'CloudFlare CDN caching'); free tier inherits the CF-backed delivery. Free egress is genuinely not the constraint here.

record.tooling: `cachix` CLI (push/use), Nix `--substituters`, and the standard Nix binary-cache HTTP protocol (narinfo/nar). No rclone backend but the nar protocol is scriptable.
record.chaining: one cache per account, 5 GB free; unlimited free accounts x 5 GB. Because a Nix cache is content-addressed and deduplicated, identical NARs are only stored once per cache - so multiplication is by account, not by file.
record.limits_note: per-account quota: 5 GB hard on free (open-source only). retention: garbage collection removes unreferenced paths after a retention window (docs have a dedicated GC page). request-rate: not documented; served via Cloudflare.
record.reliability_note: Clean, documented, Cloudflare-fronted, unlimited bandwidth - the 5 GB is the only issue, and it is 100x short of the workload. Any Nix-cache-based plan is account-farming at 5 GB/account.

evidence.proved: 'Users have a free 5 GB limit for open source projects and 20 Cachix Deploy agents'; '50 GiB of storage / Unlimited bandwidth / CloudFlare CDN caching' on Starter
probe: GET -> 200, 241 bytes (cache endpoint live, anonymous)
